svg.title: The standard stabilization of channel trace-distance discrimination permits restriction to positive joint inputs. Hence half the diamond distance between MP and D is at most 2/3. A Fourier eigenstate gives deterministic versus uniform labels and attains this value. Scaling by |h1 −h2|/2 proves the theorem’s distance. For the common purification |Ω⟩= 3−1/2 P i |i⟩S|i⟩R, the output pointer/reference block is Ej(h)T /3. Its difference is (h1 −h2)(P T j −I/3)/6. Since ∥Pj −I/3∥1 = 4/3, the sum of the three block norms gives the same half trace distance |h1 −h2|/3. One can attain it by measuring the reference in the conjugate Fourier basis and comparing that outcome with the pointer. All preparations, reference basis and decoding are fixed independently of which candidate source is used. The equal passive laws and resource counts follow from the original family theorem.
